seoTitle: llms-full.txt Builder: Combine Pages into One File
metaDescription: Combine pasted page contents into a single llms-full.txt with a title, summary and a heading and source line per page. Free, in your browser.
intro: Concatenates your pages into one Markdown file with consistent headings and source lines.
why:
Some sites publish llms-full.txt, the full text of their documentation in one file, so a model or tool can load it in one go. There is no strict format, so the useful part is consistency: one heading per page and where it came from.

Separate your pages with a line like === URL | Title, and the tool builds the file, optionally stripping HTML tags and turning headings into Markdown. It does not decide what is worth including.
howTo: Paste pages with a === URL | Title line before each.
Set the site name and summary.

faq.a: No. llms.txt is a proposal and llms-full.txt is a common companion, with no fixed structure.
It removes tags and keeps headings, lists and paragraphs as plain Markdown.
Some do; there is no guarantee.
